solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hoarder, one hopping between branches?

definitions.meaning: someone who stashes things away against future need
a bushy-tailed rodent that leaps from bough to bough

explanation.walkthrough: To squirrel away is to hoard, so a hoarder is nicknamed after the tree-dwelling rodent of the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a habitual stasher of possessions, and the agile tree-dwelling rodent that buries nuts.

clue.text: Article in press surprisingly thinly based

indicators.note: in puts the article inside the word press
surprisingly hints at an unexpected arrangement of the letters

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An article in the press is surprisingly short on evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives PRAESS or similar, which 'surprisingly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty and thinly scattered, which fits something thinly based.

clue.text: Improvement at college with shift

parts.note: being up means being in residence at university
a turn is a shift or spell of work

explanation.surface: Things get better at university with a change of work hours.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at Oxford or Cambridge means in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: A rise in fortunes, a synonym of improvement.

clue.text: Artist beginning to transmit work of giant dramatist

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the first letter of transmit
work of tells us the letters of giant are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A painter starts broadcasting the creations of a huge playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work of' rearranges GIANT into TIGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence, the English playwright of The Winslow Boy, an example of a dramatist.

clue.text: Whirlwind characterised dynamo in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A whirlwind is described as a dynamo, at least partly.
explanation.definitionFit: A swirling current of air or water, loosely a small whirlwind.

clue.text: Composer from Australia in vehicle reversing

indicators.note: in puts the Australia abbreviation inside the turned vehicle
reversing tells us the vehicle word is read from right to left

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle running on rails
Oz is the informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: A musician who hails from Australia travels in a van that is backing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolfgang Amadeus is the classical Austrian composer, an example of the class named.

clue.text: Troop wandering around old city

indicators.note: around places the scrambled troop letters about the letter for old
wandering suggests the letters roam into a new order

explanation.surface: Soldiers roam about an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges TROOP; 'around' sets those letters about O.
explanation.definitionFit: Porto, Portugal's second city, takes this older English form.

clue.text: Make known part of speech in a new church

indicators.note: in places the part of speech inside the other pieces

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a noun is a part of speech

explanation.surface: Telling the congregation about grammar in a new church.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim or declare publicly, a synonym of make known.

clue.text: Train cut after changes? I'm disinclined to speak

definitions.note: the definition is a self-description; the adjective is what such a speaker is

indicators.note: after changes means once altered, so the letters of train cut are rearranged

explanation.surface: A passenger whose train is cut after changes refuses to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserved and saying little, describing someone unwilling to talk.

clue.text: Put a diet under review indicating intelligence

indicators.note: something under review is being reconsidered and reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dieting plan being reassessed as a sign of how clever someone is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under review' rearranges PUTADIET; 'indicating' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural aptness or ability, a synonym for intelligence or talent.

clue.text: Unimportant employee put back container for drink

parts.note: a cog in the machine is a minor worker

indicators.note: put back signals the container word is turned around

parts.note: a can is a container

explanation.surface: A lowly worker returns a container meant for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' turns CAN into NAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy from the French region is a well-known example of a drink.

clue.text: Four books kept by friend crucially important

indicators.note: kept by means held inside, so the four-and-books piece goes inside friend

parts.note: a pal is a friend
IV is four in Roman numerals
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A friend keeping four books is vital.
explanation.definitionFit: Central to how things turn out, a synonym for crucially important.

clue.text: Foul discord erupted with no end of panic

indicators.note: erupted suggests something bursting apart, so the letters of discord are scrambled
with no signals that a letter is to be removed from the fodder
end of picks out the final letter of the word panic

explanation.surface: A nasty quarrel broke out, and nobody panicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes C ('end of' panic) from DISCORD, leaving DISORD, which 'erupted' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Squalid and morally base, so a close synonym of foul.

clue.text: Young woman bound, we hear, to produce doubt

indicators.note: we hear tells us the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: a young woman is a miss, and bound means trussed

explanation.surface: A tied-up girl prompts suspicion.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of trust, a synonym of doubt or suspicion.

clue.text: Unproductive part of Leicester, I learnt

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a barren area of Leicester.
explanation.walkthrough: Leicester is an English city in the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren and unable to produce, a synonym of unproductive.

clue.text: One sitting in car in outskirts of Croydon gets warning

indicators.note: in places the car-and-one group between the outer letters of Croydon
outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters of Croydon
sitting in puts the numeral for one inside the car word

parts.note: auto is a short word for car
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone sitting in a car on the edge of Croydon receives a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: Croydon is a town in south London. 'sitting in' gives AUTIO; 'in' places that between C and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal warning, such as one given by police, is a caution.

clue.text: Mark second estate, say

parts.note: an estate is a type of car, so the 'say' marks an example

explanation.surface: A grader marks a second housing estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A mark left on skin by a healed wound, a synonym.

clue.text: Normal names manufactured cheese

parts.note: par is the normal or average standard

indicators.note: manufactured means made up, so the letters of names are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Ordinary brand names produced for a cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufactured' rearranges NAMES into MESAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard Italian grating cheese is an example of a cheese.

clue.text: Support grabbed by young chap — or a dog

indicators.note: grabbed by means held, so the support piece goes inside the young chap

parts.note: a lad is a young chap
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A youngster grabs a support, or perhaps a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The retriever breed is an example of a dog.

clue.text: Same lout disrupted partner?

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A disruptive lout as someone's other half?
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal romantic partner, the question mark noting a perfect match.

clue.text: A grate partly open

parts.note: to grate on someone is to jar on them

explanation.surface: A fireplace grate stands half open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grate' looks like a fireplace noun, but it is the verb meaning to irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: A door slightly open is described this way, the standard synonym.

clue.text: Traitor's principal cause

indicators.note: principal means first in line, so the first letter of the word Traitor's

parts.note: a reason is a cause

explanation.surface: The main motive of someone who betrays their country.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: betraying the state is what a traitor principally does.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayal of one's country is the central offence that defines a traitor.

clue.text: Woman, a delightful person largely with funny hat

indicators.note: largely means most of, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a gas is slang for a fun, delightful person
the final letter dropped

indicators.note: funny means odd, so the letters of hat are scrambled

explanation.surface: A woman, a charming person mostly, in a silly hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' trims GAS to GA; 'funny' turns HAT into THA.
explanation.definitionFit: A female given name, as of crime writer Christie, so an example of a woman.

clue.text: A craft that relies on current power?

definitions.text: A craft that relies on current power?

parts.words: A craft that relies on current power?
parts.note: current suggests electricity, but here it means air currents lifting an engineless aircraft

explanation.walkthrough: 'current power' suggests electricity; the craft rides air currents.
explanation.definitionFit: An engineless aircraft kept aloft by rising air currents.

clue.text: Elevation for, say, army section to come out

indicators.note: elevation means raising up, so in a down clue the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: e.g. means for example, say
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: Raising an army unit for a parade to come out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevation' reads EGREME upwards in this down clue; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To appear or come into view, a synonym of come out.

clue.text: Flower produced by a set-up in Welsh town

indicators.note: in puts the article and set-up inside the Welsh town

parts.note: Mold is a town in north-east Wales
a rig is an arrangement or set-up of equipment

explanation.surface: A bloom grown by some arrangement in a town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced by' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright orange garden bloom, an example of a flower.

clue.text: Race going downhill? Nothing in mall's organised

indicators.note: in puts the nought inside the letters of mall's
organised means arranged into order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word taken with its s as letters
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A shopping centre arranges a race heading downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' gives MALOLS, which 'organised' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A zigzag ski race down a course of gates, defined playfully as a downhill race.

clue.text: Manage company drills

parts.note: PE, physical education, is exercise drills

explanation.surface: Running a business with regular drills.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to handle a difficulty successfully or get by.

clue.text: Staid scribe discontented girlfriend?

indicators.note: discontented read as 'contents removed' leaves only the first and last letters of scribe

parts.note: a date is someone you go out with

explanation.surface: A dull writer is unhappy with his girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' looks like 'unhappy' but means emptied of contents.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm, composed and unexcitable, a close synonym of staid.

clue.text: Lean cord getting threadbare? It's full of holes

indicators.note: fabric getting threadbare is falling apart, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: Thin corduroy wearing thin is full of holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen strainer pierced all over, so cleverly described as full of holes.

clue.text: Adamant refusal to accept right in country

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: no way is a firm refusal

explanation.surface: A firm refusal to admit someone into a country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scandinavian kingdom is an example of a country.

clue.text: What those on boards do hidden from view?

definitions.text: What those on boards do hidden from view?

parts.words: What those on boards do hidden from view?
parts.note: actors, those on the boards of a stage, practise privately before the audience arrives

explanation.walkthrough: 'The boards' is the stage, so those on boards are actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors practise a play in private before performing, which is what this verb means.
